reviewedBy: Oza (repository owner), accepting the automated code audit's findings on 2026-07-28. Prepared by the audit; reviewed and accepted by the owner.
reason: tunisia/tn-paye.html was modelling the wrong country. It computed a fund it called CNPS at 2.5% employee / 9.5% employer, and ran a tax scale of 0% to TND 300,000 then 2%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 20% and 25% above TND 9,600,000. CNPS is the Caisse Nationale de Prevoyance Sociale, which is Cote d'Ivoire's and Cameroon's fund, not Tunisia's; the FAQ even expanded the acronym that way. Those band thresholds are XOF magnitudes, not dinars - TND 300,000 is not a plausible tax-free threshold. The page was a copy of an Ivorian calculator with the country name changed. It also disagreed with itself: the _grossToNet helper already read a 'cnss' toggle and applied 9.18%, while the visible calculator applied 2.5% through a 'cnps' toggle, so the two paths on one page produced different numbers. Corrected to Tunisia's actual regime. Fund: CNSS (Caisse Nationale de Securite Sociale). Employee contribution 9.68% and employer 17.07% - the long-standing private non-agricultural rates of 9.18% and 16.57% plus the 0.5% each added by the Finance Law 2025 for the new Unemployment Insurance Fund, per PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, which reports the combined 9.68%/17.07% figures. Income tax: the IRPP scale introduced by the Finance Law 2025 and in force from 1 January 2025 - 0% to TND 5,000; 15% to 10,000; 25% to 20,000; 30% to 30,000; 33% to 40,000; 36% to 50,000; 38% to 70,000; 40% above 70,000 - plus the Social Solidarity Contribution of 0.5% on the same taxable income for FY2023-2026 (1% from 2027). Verified by hand at TND 30,000 annual gross: CNSS 2,904; taxable 27,096; IRPP 750 + 2,500 + 2,128.80 = 5,378.80; CSS 135.48; total tax 5,514.28; net 21,581.72. The toggle id in markup, the _grossToNet helper, the band card, the comparison table, the hero badges, the meta descriptions, the FAQ JSON-LD and the visible FAQ were all updated to match; a grep for CNPS and for the 2.5%/9.5% rates now returns zero. The Swahili translation at sw/egypt-style route sw/tunisia/kikokotoo-kodi-mshahara already used CNSS at the correct 9.18%/16.57% and Tunisia's pre-2025 IRPP scale, so it was the more faithful implementation; it has been brought to the same current figures, and an unsourced TND 1,200 blanket relief it carried was removed. Recorded gap on both pages: Tunisia's professional-expenses deduction is still not modelled.
